transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-07-21
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 39 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jules Kim (Redwood SE), Martin Hu (CTO, ArborLink), Priya Rao (Head of Cloud Eng, ArborLink), Evan Torres (Platform Architect, ArborLink)

Auto-generated summary (optional): discussed onramp options and initial constraints; follow-ups assigned

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Samir with Redwood Inference, AE on the account. Quick intro round-robin?
[00:08] Martin: Hi I'm Martin, CTO at ArborLink, we run a hybrid cloud for geospatial analytics and have a lot of edge clusters in EU and NA.
[00:16] Priya: Priya, cloud lead, mostly focused on compliance and deployment automation.
[00:22] Evan: Evan, platform, I own the infra templates and GPU ops.
[00:26] Jules: Jules from Redwood, I'm the SE, I'll dig into the technical details and help set up benchmarks.

[02:05] Samir: Cool — goal for today is a technical intro to scope a hybrid onramp: private deployment in their VPC and a Dedicated option we can provide. High level constraints, timeline, success criteria.
[02:18] Priya: Timeline is relatively tight, we want a pilot in Q3, ideally a small POC in 6 weeks. Success is 1) match latency targets for inference under 120ms p95 for our typical 512-token prompts, 2) cost floor under our current spend, and 3) certifications — SOC2 and KMS integration.
[02:45] Jules: Understood. Quick question on hardware — what's in your edge clusters?
[02:52] Evan: We're running a mix: most nodes are LodeCore-2 blades with Ampere A100-equivalent cards, some older V100s for batch offline, and a few newly ordered H100-ish blades for larger models.
[03:10] Jules: Okay, good, that maps well to Redwood's runtime which supports mixed quantized paths. We may need to adjust kernel selection and quantization per model. Also, does ArborLink prefer the private control plane or a VPC tethered Redwood private option?

[04:00] Martin: We can't host the control plane in your cloud — data residency rules mean control plane metadata must remain inside our network. So we're looking at Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem package) or a customer-managed control plane.
[04:15] Samir: Totally expected. We have a private deployment that ships a control plane agent and can be run in a customer's VPC with keys staying on-prem. There's an on-prem installer but we usually start with a VPC deployment. We'll share the installer checklist.
[04:40] Priya: KMS — we use HashiCorp Vault in our VPC with HSM wrapping. How does Redwood integrate?
[04:47] Jules: We support customer KMS via KMIP and have an HSM-integrated key wrapping flow; sometimes the transcript in the doc says K M S as separate but it's KMS. We'll need to validate with your Vault team. Can you share the Vault endpoint and any proxying details?

[06:00] Evan: Also curious about networking: do you require VPC peering or transit? Our clusters are on our own fabric with IP ranges that change across sites.
[06:12] Jules: We can do VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, or a VPN tunnel. For multi-site we often recommend a local control plane per region with gRPC tunnels back for telemetry. Peering vs Transit Gateway depends on scale; we can diagram options.

[07:30] Martin: From a performance perspective, we need to ensure token latency and KV cache behavior in our runtime. How does Redwood handle KV cache eviction across mixed GPU types?
[07:45] Jules: Good question — our runtime maintains local KV cache per replica and uses a consistency window for warm starts; on heterogeneous clusters we pick placement to keep KV hot on the fastest device class. There can be slight variance in p95 if requests cross-device boundaries. We can run profiling to show expected p95 distribution.
[08:20] Samir: For the POC we can run a tracer and provide per-route latency breakdowns; we'll include token-level cost estimates so you can compare.

[09:00] Priya: Security: audit logs, RBAC, and SSO. We require SAML-based SSO, fine grained RBAC, and 90 day log retention for audit trails.
[09:12] Jules: Redwood Private supports SAML SSO and can forward audit logs to your SIEM via syslog or direct CloudWatch ingestion. Retention can be configured on your side; we can ship forwarders. We'll attach the SOC2 evidence pack.
[09:40] Samir: Note that our SOC2 and ISO docs are public but we do have customer-specific attestations on request — we'll include the attestation timeline.

[11:00] Evan: On model support — we'll likely run Llama-style and some Llama 2 forks plus a reranker. Any compile or kernel constraints I should know about?
[11:12] Jules: Runtime supports transformer families; compilation chooses kernels based on seq length and batch. For Llama forks we generally need a minor tokenization check and may recommend loaded quantized weights. If you plan to run >8k context we should verify memory across A100/H100 shapes.
[11:45] Martin: Okay. For the benchmark, our key metrics are p95 latency for 512 tokens, throughput for batch size 8, and cost per 1M tokens. Also cold start behavior for short-lived lambdas at edge sites.
[12:05] Jules: We can script the benchmark to hit those exact profiles. We'll need a sample prompt set and some representative traces; can your team share a small dataset (anonymized) and peak QPS expectations?

[13:00] Priya: Yes, we can scrub and share 1k sample prompts and QPS profiles; also note some of our nodes are behind NAT and not directly routable.
[13:10] Samir: That's fine; we can run an agent that initiates outbound connections so no inbound rules needed. We'll document network ports and egress requirements.

[15:00] Evan: What's the deployment path? Installer, Docker images, or kube helm charts?
[15:08] Jules: We provide a Kubernetes helm chart and an on-prem operator for air-gapped installs. Installer artifacts include image tarballs, manifests, and a quickstart script. For VPC mode we use helm and a small agent.

[17:00] Martin: Cost question — we like Dedicated for predictable capacity but want burst into hosted to avoid overprovisioning. How does billing and accounting happen across those modes?
[17:15] Samir: Typically commit to a Dedicated pool for baseline and burst into our hosted offering billed per token at a slightly higher rate. We'll provide a model showing unit economics and token routing rules; you can pin routes by priority or region.

[18:30] Priya: Legal/procurement: we need an initial SOW and on-prem license terms. Who on Redwood handles that?
[18:40] Samir: I'll own the SOW and loop legal. For pilots we do a time-boxed PO or an MSA + SOW depending on procurement needs. We'll include standard IP and data clauses.

[20:00] Evan: Any concerns about driver versions for Ampere vs Nvidia? We run Container Toolkit and a mix of driver stacks.
[20:12] Jules: We recommend uniform drivers per cluster and can provide a compatibility matrix. For A100-class vs H100-class there are different CUDA/ROCm paths; our runtime supports containerized driver layers but operator will want to pin kernel modules.

[22:30] Samir: Let's frame the POC: 1) Redwood runs benchmarks (Jules leads) on a small set of your nodes or we can provision a test cluster, 2) security review concurrently (Samir) with docs, 3) pricing sketch (Samir) and 4) schedule follow-up in two weeks. Any objections?
[22:52] Martin: Sounds good. For the benchmark we prefer Redwood run it on our hardware if possible; if not we'll run the left side and share results.
[23:10] Jules: We can do remote or on-site. For remote we need secure access or an agent and the samples. I'll craft a benchmark playbook.

[25:00] Priya: Also can you share any previous perf numbers on similar LodeCore nodes? A ballpark helps with procurement.
[25:12] Jules: I have internal runs on LodeCore-class hardware — I'll redact customer names and share aggregated numbers.

[27:00] Samir: Next steps recap — we'll send VPC diagram and installer checklist, Jules will send benchmark plan, share SOC2/ISO docs, and provide pricing sketch. We'll set a follow-up for 2025-08-04 at 10am PT. Does that work?
[27:25] Martin: Yes works.

[28:00] Evan: Quick question about telemetry — is tracing sampled or full? We need to ensure PII isn't leaked.
[28:12] Jules: Telemetry is sampled by default; sensitive payloads can be redacted at the agent. We'll document data fields that are logged and provide an option to disable payload logging.

[30:00] Priya: One more compliance question: we have sites in EU with data residency constraints — can control plane metadata remain in EU only?
[30:12] Samir: Yes, we can run regional control planes or a local control plane per region. For PII you'd want local policy enforcement. We'll capture that in the deployment diagram.

[32:00] Martin: Any competitors we should be aware of? We've been looking at LambdaCloud and Infragrid — your differentiator?
[32:12] Samir: We position on production economics and unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private; also deep focus on transparent benchmarks and rollout tooling. Not perfect fit for every use case but lots of ops-level tooling.

[34:00] Priya: Ok thanks. I'll coordinate internal stakeholders for the SSO and Vault details.
[34:12] Evan: I'll pull sample prompts and a node inventory.

[35:00] Samir: Great — Jules, can you confirm benchmark artifacts you'll need?
[35:08] Jules: Sure — sample prompt set (anonymized), target QPS, node inventory (GPU types, driver versions), network topology (NAT details), and a contact with Vault admin. I'll put a checklist in the follow-up email.

[36:30] Martin: Any wrinkles around licensing for on-prem images? We need entitlements tied to node counts.
[36:40] Samir: Our Private license can be per-node or capacity-based; we'll propose both models in the sketch.

[38:00] Closing
[38:05] Samir: Thanks all, we'll circulate notes and set the follow-up for Aug 4. Jules and I will share the checklist and pricing sketch within the week.
[38:18] Priya: Thanks everyone.
[38:22] Martin: Thanks.
[38:25] Jules: Bye.

End of transcript (auto-transcribed, occasional mis-heard words and speaker overlaps).
